cases.question: How many litres does the fuel tank hold, and roughly how much is left when the low fuel warning comes on?
cases.reference_answer: Fuel tank capacity 17.0* L; Low fuel warning 3 L ± 0.5* L (p18). The asterisk note says: 'The above values are approximate and the actual fuel filling capacity will vary from the values mentioned.' (Dead stock is listed as 0.95 L to 1.15* L, p18.) Low fuel is shown by the last segment of the 4-segment fuel bar blinking with the low fuel tell tale ON (p63). WARNING (p64): do not use the motorcycle for long duration with the fuel indication in last segment blinking; refuel at the earliest, otherwise it can run out of fuel, leave you stranded and cause serious damage to the fuel pump.

cases.question: How long is the standard warranty on the Himalayan 450, and does it carry over if I sell the bike?
cases.reference_answer: General warranty (p129): 'Warranty for any Motorcycle shall be in force until the expiry of 36months or 30,000 km, whichever comes first from the date of the Sale of the motorcycle to the first owner and to any subsequent owners for the balance of the remaining period'. To avail warranty benefits, the second or subsequent owner should inform the nearest Royal Enfield Service Centre about the purchase and fill in the requisite details in the form requested (p129). The warranty applies only if all maintenance and services are availed within the warranty period/kilometer ranges per the owner's manual schedule from a Royal Enfield Authorized Dealer/Service Centre (p130).
must_include: 36 months or 30,000 km, whichever comes first
runs from date of sale; later owners get the balance of the period
new owner must inform the nearest Royal Enfield Service Centre and fill in the form

A.released_text: The standard (general) warranty lasts until 36 months or 30,000 km, whichever comes first, from the sale to the first owner. cases.question: How do I check the engine oil level correctly?
cases.reference_answer: Engine oil level checking (p83): place the vehicle upright on a level surface; start the engine from cold condition, let it idle for 2 to 3 minutes and stop the engine; wait 2 to 3 minutes for the oil to settle and assess the sight glass (the oil level window is on the right side, p24). cases.question: My bike tipped over with the engine running and it cut out. How do I reset it so it starts again?
cases.reference_answer: Roll over sensor (p68): if the motorcycle falls over on either side with the engine running and gears engaged, the roll over sensor disables the fuel systems and switches OFF the engine. To reset it and reactivate the fuel systems: ensure the motorcycle is made upright and is on its center stand; ensure gears are in correct neutral and the neutral lamp is glowing in the instrument console; switch OFF both ignition and stop switches, wait for a few seconds, and switch ON the ignition and stop switch again to start the engine. Optional: to find neutral, move the motorcycle back and forth gently while shifting (p72); CAUTION (p75) do not attempt to shift gears without moving the motorcycle back and forth as it will damage the gears mechanism.

cases.question: My coolant looks low. How do I top it up, and which coolant should I use?
cases.reference_answer: Coolant: TOTAL COOLELF AUTO SUPRA -37 ºC; coolant from Total is ready to use and does not require mixing (p21, p87). Expansion tank: fill to max mark - 200 ml (p21). Check coolant level in the expansion tank every 1000 km (or earlier as required) and top up as required (p125). Topping up: remove the radiator expansion tank cap, fill the tank to the upper level line and replace the cap (p87). Full fill/air bleeding (p86-87): vehicle straight on ground level; remove the radiator pressure cap and fill up to the filler neck; air bleed by gently tapping and squeezing both engine-to-radiator hoses and tipping the bike approximately 45-60 degrees left then right, topping back up to the filler neck until the level no longer drops; refit the radiator pressure cap fully tightened clockwise; fill the expansion tank to the upper level line; start in neutral, idle 5 minutes, blip throttle 3 or 4 times, stop and let it cool, top up the expansion tank if required, and check for leaks. NOTE: do not fill coolant with the vehicle on the side stand (p87). WARNING (p86): never open a radiator cap when the engine is hot; released pressure can make coolant boil and spurt out, causing severe burns. WARNING (p87): do not spill coolant; collect it and dispose through authorized agencies; avoid skin contact and wash affected area with soap and water.

cases.question: When removing the battery, which terminal do I disconnect first, and which one goes back on first?

cases.question: How do I check the brake fluid level, and what fluid should I top up with?
cases.reference_answer: Checking brake fluid (p88): place the motorcycle upright on a firm, level surface. Front: check that the reservoir is horizontal and the fluid level is at the center of the window (considered the minimum level). Rear: check that the reservoir is horizontal and the level is between the 'MAX' and 'Min' marks. The pre-ride check says the level must be above the 'MIN' mark (p70). Fluid: DOT 4 (p21). NOTES (p88-89): clean the filler cap before removing; use only DOT 4 brake fluid from sealer container; use only the specified fluid or seals may deteriorate and leak; refill with the same type - adding fluid other than DOT 4 may cause a harmful chemical reaction; keep water and dust out (water lowers the boiling point and may cause vapor lock; dirt may clog ABS hydraulic unit valves). CAUTION (p88): brake fluid is highly corrosive and damages painted parts - clean any spill immediately with a soft (preferably wet) cloth; do not mix DOT 4 and other brake fluid. WARNING (p89): insufficient brake fluid level will cause the brake system to fail; old fluid reduces braking effect; change front and rear fluid per the periodic maintenance schedule (replace at 20,000 km/24 months and 40,000 km/48 months, p127); keep brake fluid out of reach of children and away from skin, eyes and clothing.

cases.question: How full should I fill the fuel tank when refuelling?
cases.reference_answer: Fill only to the bottom of the anti splash plate, not to the brim, leaving air space for fuel expansion (p8, p27; filling-level diagram shows fuel filler collar, anti splash plate and maximum fuel level, p28). Refuelling guidelines (p8): switch OFF mobile phones; no smoking, open flames or sparks; refuel in a well ventilated area with the engine turned off; open the tank cap slowly. Cap (p27): lift the key flap, insert key, turn clockwise to open; press the cap to lock with the key in position; remove key and close flap. WARNING (p27): do not overfill; fill only till the bottom of the anti splash plate; overfilling may let gasoline enter the EVAP canister and damage the evaporative emission system. CAUTION (p27): gasoline vapour is highly explosive - no flames or sparks, ventilated area only, no smoking while refuelling or with the cap open; wipe off any fuel spilled on painted surfaces immediately as it may leave a permanent stain. Optional: the fuel indicator refreshes after refuelling once the side stand is retracted and ignition is turned ON (p63).

cases.question: A fuse blew mid-ride. Can I just bridge it with a bit of wire or foil to get home?
cases.reference_answer: No. WARNING (p112): 'Any attempt to jumper a defective fuse gives rise to the risk of a short-circuit and fire. Always replace a defective fuse with a new fuse of the same rating.' Usage of fuses other than the specified rating, any other conductive materials or low grade fuses will damage the complete electrical system. Instead use a spare: the fuse box holds SF1 Yellow 5 A, SF2 Red 10 A, SF3 Blue 15 A (p112); the fuse carrier is underneath the rider seat (remove pillion and rider seats, p111); a fuse puller is in the tool kit (p81); keep the ignition OFF when replacing fuses (p112). Replace the used spare at the earliest opportunity, and get the electrical system checked and faults corrected immediately after any fuse failure, or fuses may keep failing (p112). Troubleshooting: replace the fuse with same rating; contact an Authorised service center if the problem persists (p121).

cases.question: My ABS light stays on even above 5 km/h. Is it okay to keep riding for a few weeks before getting it checked?

Do's (p69) and troubleshooting (p122) likewise say to take it to / contact an Authorised service centre. The manual does not identify the cause; the answer must not guess one.
